details:
hs-framework 999.9.1 and 999.9.2 (published by the npm account ls123test123 on 2026-10-28) carry no code of their own: index.js only logs a line. Their single dependency, ltidisafe, is fetched from a URL outside the registry (https://storage.googleapis.com/lscunpentest/pack_ux_foundry.tgz in 999.9.1, .../pack_npm_new.tgz in 999.9.2; both files are the same archive, SHA-256 e4df56e338a8bb31b0595e64ace3b0a60650d50ccefb9f6b942c0a885432f30f). That archive declares `"preinstall": "node test.js > /dev/null 2>&1"`. test.js (SHA-256 dab39b79cd75cd5fb3ae546ea074c1bf5673e74e930474ce79e117b05c06bb0d) reads the machine's IPv4 addresses, os.hostname() and os.homedir(), hex-encodes the last two, and sends each as a subdomain of 2227msddk3ts19p2n1g239dhj8pydn.oastify.com, a Burp Collaborator address, so the data leaves with the DNS lookup and the HTTP request. The high version number is typical of dependency confusion.

Found by Gatekeeper (https://github.com/lb2002/gatekeeper); read statically from the published archive and the dependency's archive, never executed.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
